newsitem.title: USA: NY State Sen disappointed by MSRB pay-to-play vote.
newsitem.headline: NY State Sen disappointed by MSRB pay-to-play vote.

text.p: New York State Senator Franz Leichter said Tuesday that the MSRB passed up a "tremendous opportunity" to curb pay-to-play by deciding not to regulate dealer contributions to political parties.

"The Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board looked at a glaring loophole in G-37 and decided to look away," Leichter said following a board press briefing early Tuesday to announce results of a quarterly meeting July 30 to August 1.
The 15-member board voted to make information about dealer contributions to political parties more widely available by publishing it over the MSRB's Internet website.
But it opted not to amend its pay-to-play rule G-37 by adding party contributions to the list of dealer activities that can trigger a ban under the April 1994 rule.
Enacted in April 1994, rule G-37 bars broker dealers who contribute to issuer clients from doing negotiated bond business with those localties for two years afterward.

Leichter, a Democrat from the Bronx, issued two reports this year charging that securities firms sidestep MSRB's rule G-37 by making big contributions to political parties, to federal "soft-money" accounts, and to committees set up to promote state ballot initiatives.

"We can expect pay-to-play to remain alive and well because municipal bond underwriters can make contributions to political parties and gain all the advantages of a campaign donation to the governor or other state officials," Leichter said.
Leichter said he is glad that MSRB decided to put securities firms G-37 filings on the Internet, but is "extremely doubtful" that this will have any effect on pay-to-play.
